QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Landscape and Types_2

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah rotates capital into unlisted pre-IPO shares purely on the basis of 'market buzz', without any business valuation or IC memo, hoping to flip within weeks. The CIO of Saraswati Growth Fund (a Cat II AIF) reviews the activity. Which statement BEST describes this activity under the investment-vs-speculation framework described in the chapter?

answer.text: It is speculation, as risk is undertaken not commensurate with return in anticipation of gain, with minimal research into true value.
It is investment, because the holding is in equity of a real operating company.
It is investment, as any unlisted equity exposure is long-term by nature.
It is arbitrage, because it exploits the price gap between unlisted and IPO price.

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter defines speculation as forming a theory or conjecture without firm evidence — undertaking risk not commensurate with return in anticipation of higher gains, with minimum research on true value. Investment, by contrast, involves determining the intrinsic value of the asset and buying when that value exceeds the market price. Ms. Shah performs no valuation and trades on rumour — textbook speculation, regardless of the asset class or holding period. The Trap: (B) and (C) use the instrument (equity/unlisted) as the test, but the chapter explicitly warns that short vs long horizon is not a reliable investment/speculation divider. (D) Arbitrage requires two offsetting, locked-in prices — rumour-driven directional bets are not arbitrage. Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst) emphasises valuation-backed recommendations. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) treats hedge-fund style speculation more explicitly — but even at Cat III, hedge activity must be research-driven. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) enforces the same distinction in PM mandates. Manager's Pro-Tip: A Cat II AIF's IC charter should require a written valuation memo (DCF, comps, transaction multiples) for every investment approval. Treat any 'rumour-driven' pitch as a governance red flag — the chapter's speculation definition is your first line of defence against LP suitability claims later.
